To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“PWEI could support a patient-centered Web design of information and of healthcare services, and could therefore be useful in order to benchmark the Web strategies of healthcare organizations”.

(a) a Patient Web Empowering Index has been developed and tested in a sample of 340 Italian National Health Service hospitals, (b) the index was used to evaluate yearly, from 2009 to2011, the maturity of the web strategies of these hospitals, and (c) the results show that, despite the fact that the web is a key tool for the patient empowerment, the web strategies are still immature, and the accent is still on the structure of the organization, rather
the PWEI is an effective tool for assessing the degree of patient empowerment of the Web strategies of healthcare organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an instrument that could support the process of change in the health organizations, by helping them to understand the key factors for an effective patient empowerment through their web strategies.
the development of a tool for assessing the degree of patient empowerment within the INHS web sites.
the issue of patient-centered web strategies and the related impact on patient empowerment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PWEI, as a benchmarking tool, is a valuable instrument in order to support the web strategies of healthcare organizations in their effort to improve the quality of care through patient-centered web strategies.

the Web strategies of the Italian National Health Services (INHS) basically reflect a state deep immaturity and still display a tendency, all too frequently placed all on the structures and the responsibilities of the organization itself, rather than the needs of citizens and patients.
, in the context of the Italian INHS, the patient empowerment through the Web is still at an early stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) PWEI could be a useful tool in order to benchmark and evaluate the degree of maturity of the Web strategies of healthcare organizations, (2) PWEI can be used to measure the degree to which the web strategies of healthcare organizations can empower patients, (3) PWEI has been used to measure the current state of the web strategies of Italian NHS hospitals and it has been found that they display a state of deep maturity, (4) PWEI is a valid

PWEI can be used to evaluate and compare the degree of patient web empowerment of health organizations and it can be used to identify areas for improvement and to monitor the progress of web strategy.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the web strategy should be designed with the patient in mind, not with the organization.
a web site is not a mere communication channel, but rather a powerful tool for patient empowerment.
patient empowerment is not just a buzzword, but a real issue that healthcare providers should address.
